message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds any portion. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control). | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or letter) of any needed repairs.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or pursue a **repair‑and‑deduct** claim in small‑claims court. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are **reasonable** (no more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Keep receipts or bank records. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month‑to‑month**: Either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• **Fixed‑term**: The lease ends automatically unless renewed or extended. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail) to the landlord. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any harassment or unlawful entry. | | **Landlord Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., Section 8). | • File a complaint with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR). | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, you may deduct the cost of repair from your rent (up to the amount of the rent). | • Keep receipts and provide a written notice to the landlord before deducting. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must follow the Texas **eviction procedure**: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease termination), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court order. | • Respond to the lawsuit, attend the hearing, and present evidence (e.g., proof of rent payment). | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has **no statewide rent‑control laws**. | • However, local ordinances may apply in certain cities (e.g., Austin, Houston). Check local regulations. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify which utilities you are responsible for. | • Verify the lease and keep utility bills as proof of payment. | | **Insurance** | • Landlords may require renters’ insurance. | • Obtain coverage that protects your personal property and liability. | | **Subletting** | • The lease may allow or prohibit subletting. | • Obtain written permission if required. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlords must maintain common areas (hallways, elevators, parking). | • Report issues promptly. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If your rights are violated, you can:
1. File a complaint with TDHCA or HUD.
2. Seek mediation or arbitration.
3. File a civil suit for damages or injunction. | • Keep all documentation (emails, texts, photos, receipts). | --- #### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand the terms, rent amount, security deposit limits, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts help protect your rights. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with Texas Property Code §§ 92.001–92.019 (security deposits), § 92.011 (habitability), and § 92.015 (notice requirements). 4. **Communicate in Writing** – Whenever possible, use email or certified mail to keep a record. 5. **Seek Help Early** – If you encounter a problem, contact TDHCA, HUD, or a local tenant‑rights organization before it escalates. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Consumer protection, landlord‑tenant dispute resolution. | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | Fair housing complaints, tenant rights information. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** | Discrimination complaints. | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Groups** | e.g., Austin Tenants Union, Houston Tenant Advocacy. | | **Legal Aid Organizations** | Free or low‑cost legal assistance for tenants. | --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, fair treatment, and clear procedures for rent, security deposits, and eviction. Keep your lease, document everything, and know where to turn if your landlord violates your rights.
